routes.title: Attach safety evidence to Belgian compute awards
brief: Propose an incident-and-evaluation appendix for Belgium's 7.4% LUMI allocation envelope.
No adoption is documented; the full quota is an upper envelope, not measured protected compute.
routes.impactRationale: Legacy compatibility placeholder only: provisional 2/2 ratings and full ordinal ranges are not new measurements. Proposed reporting could expose failures during funded AI work; neither risk reduction nor the AI share of this quota is measured.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Legacy compatibility placeholder only, with no inferred precision. Award terms, operator implementation and recipient acceptance must be agreed; current approval-specific alignment is unknown.
routes.actor: Belgian allocation bodies, represented operationally by VSC and CECI, working with CSC as LUMI host. Their authority to amend the whole Belgian programme remains unverified.
routes.obligor: Participating recipient organisation and its PI/users; CSC would implement only the agreed service-side checks.
routes.instrument: Proposed prospective award appendix plus compatible LUMI service terms. The existing Terms of Use are a contractual starting point, not evidence that this appendix is adopted.
routes.safeguard: Require an AI-use declaration; for in-scope work, a pre-run evaluation plan, incident notification, retained evidence and evaluation access under agreed confidentiality protections. Define scope and acceptance criteria before award.
routes.verification: Pilot one consenting recipient: allocator checks the signed appendix; CSC's designated internal reviewer checks the evaluation record and exercises a simulated incident report. Record actual covered allocation separately from the 7.4% envelope.
routes.remedy: Negotiate a proportionate pause-and-cure procedure for appendix breaches. Existing Terms section 10 concerns unauthorised use or suspected Terms breaches; it does not independently establish this proposed model-safety remedy.
routes.window: As observed 2026-10-31, Belgium lists regular cut-offs of 2 March, 1 June and 5 October 2026, all past. Preparatory/development submissions are continuous with monthly review; that is a possible pilot channel, not evidence of authority or an announced 2027 regular round.
routes.evidenceSummary: BE-ACCESS identifies the 7.4% total-time quota. LUMI-ACCESS names operational allocators and project registration. LUMI-TERMS identifies the host and existing contractual framework. No source documents acceptance of the proposed safeguard.
routes.gap: The whole-quota amendment signatories, funder approvals, binding evaluation-access rights and eligible AI usage are unknown. A small pilot cannot claim coverage of the whole Belgian quota.
routes.nextQuestion: Which Belgian decision-makers can approve a prospective appendix, and will CSC and one recipient agree to test its evidence and pause procedure?
incentives: Proposal: allocators gain auditable evidence about funded AI work.
Proposal: recipients gain a predictable evidence checklist and a defined cure process.
constraints: Belgian national control of allocation does not imply unilateral control of the Finnish host.
Recipient IP, personal data and research-publication obligations require compatible terms.
Belgium is already inside the national 50% pool; never add this route to that pool.

routes.title: Set evidence conditions on EuroHPC compute access
brief: Propose evaluation access and incident evidence across EuroHPC's half of LUMI allocation.
This is a prospective award-and-service agreement, not an existing model-safety veto.
routes.impactRationale: Legacy compatibility placeholder only: provisional 2/2 and full ordinal ranges are not new measurements. The numerical input is a quota share, not model coverage or risk reduction.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Legacy compatibility placeholder only, with no inferred precision. EuroHPC decision authority, CSC implementation and recipient acceptance are unresolved for the proposed terms.
routes.actor: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking as allocation-channel decision-maker, with CSC as operator and operational resource allocator.
routes.obligor: Consenting recipient institution and its PI/users, with CSC responsible for agreed operator-side verification.
routes.instrument: Proposed prospective EuroHPC award conditions paired with an operator-approved service appendix; the precise EuroHPC approval procedure needs verification.
routes.safeguard: For declared AI work, obtain evaluation access, a reproducible evidence package and incident notification before further agreed compute tranches. Non-AI projects would still declare applicability; the quota contains an unknown mix of workloads.
routes.verification: One-recipient pilot: EuroHPC specifies acceptance criteria, CSC's designated internal reviewer tests access to an evaluation artifact and a simulated incident record, and the recipient demonstrates correction before a proposed next tranche.
routes.remedy: Propose withholding the next agreed tranche until deficiencies are cured. This requires prospective conditions and a defined review process; neither a universal release veto nor automatic forfeiture follows from existing capacity cut-offs.
routes.window: Negotiate for a future eligible award before acceptance. The Users in Europe page lists several access modes but this review establishes no particular open amendment window or 2027 deadline.
routes.evidenceSummary: LUMI-SPLIT places half the allocation in EuroHPC's channel; EU-ACCESS identifies its access calls. LUMI-ACCESS distinguishes EuroHPC decisions from CSC's operational project role. Current safety-condition adoption is unlocated.
routes.gap: Internal EuroHPC approvals, governing allocation policy, cost of verification and authority to attach these specific conditions need checking. One consenting pilot cannot establish channel-wide adoption.
routes.nextQuestion: Will EuroHPC identify the approval instrument for prospective evaluation-access conditions and authorise CSC to trial a precisely scoped appendix with one recipient?
incentives: Proposal: one common condition could reduce inconsistent evidence requests across EuroHPC access calls.
Proposal: recipient projects get explicit acceptance criteria before committing workloads.
constraints: An EU-level institution must agree; national governments alone do not implement this route.
Work can migrate to other compute providers; substitution is unmeasured.
The 50% pool is disjoint from the national pool but is not 50% of AI training or global compute.

routes.title: Share a safety-evidence protocol across national quotas
brief: Extend the Belgian-style evidence appendix across the national half of LUMI allocation.
All national channels must participate to reach 50%; Belgium's 7.4% is already included.
routes.impactRationale: Legacy compatibility placeholder only: provisional 2/2 and full ordinal ranges are not new measurements. Shared evidence may make findings reusable across awards, but broader quota coverage does not establish better safety outcomes.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Legacy compatibility placeholder only, with no inferred precision. Multiple national policies must accommodate the same appendix; no coordination bonus or probability is assigned.
routes.actor: National LUMI allocation channels jointly, through their listed operational allocators and the yet-to-be-confirmed competent policy signatories; CSC implements agreed common service-side checks.
routes.obligor: Consenting recipient institutions and PI/users in participating national channels; shared evidence access is limited to the parties and purposes actually agreed.
routes.instrument: Proposed common prospective award appendix, retained in each national allocation policy, plus compatible CSC service terms and evidence-sharing arrangements.
routes.safeguard: Use the Belgian-route AI declaration, evaluation plan, incident evidence and evaluation-access requirements with a shared schema and acceptance criteria. Recognise prior evidence only where scope and version match; avoid automatic recognition of stale results.
routes.verification: First demonstrate one recipient's evidence package can be checked against the common schema by CSC's designated internal reviewer. Separately audit each channel's adoption and actual covered awards before claiming rollout coverage.
routes.remedy: Each adopting channel would agree its own pause-and-cure procedure; CSC implements only compatible accepted service actions. A shared schema does not create mutual legal authority or automatic cross-channel exclusion.
routes.window: Prospective national awards, on each channel's own schedule. No synchronised amendment round or common 2027 deadline was established. Belgium's continuous preparatory channel is a possible pilot, not a timetable for the coalition.
routes.evidenceSummary: LUMI-SPLIT establishes the national half and local policies. LUMI-ACCESS lists eleven national channels and operational organisations. The coalition and its shared safety appendix are proposals, with no documented adoption.
routes.gap: Operational allocator names are not a complete legal approval set. Danish university partners, consortium constituents, funder authority, recipient rights and cross-border evidence permissions require identification.
routes.nextQuestion: Can the listed allocators identify their competent signatories and agree one shared evidence schema without changing each other's award authority?
incentives: Proposal: compatible evidence packages reduce duplicate preparation when projects seek different national awards.
Proposal: allocators can compare incident handling while retaining their own award decisions.
constraints: National policies differ and each participating allocation channel needs agreement.
The 50% assumes all national channels; no sourced shares support a smaller coalition's numerical envelope here.
Belgium is nested within this pool. Pairing is a scope comparison, not a controlled experiment in coordination.
